**Driril's budget is now $1528K.** I applied the policy in two passes.

**Pass 1: settle the withdrawals.** Some withdrawals target other withdrawals, so I resolved each chain from the latest record backwards. An update stays in effect if its chain of active withdrawals is even. Examples:

- **#0004 (+$237K) stays in effect.** #0019 withdrew it, but #0114 withdrew #0019.
- **#0024 (+$502K) stays in effect.** The chain is #0566 → #0116 → #0047 → #0032. #0566 cancels #0116, so #0047 stands and cancels #0032.
- **#0014 (−$222K) is withdrawn.** The chain is #0532 → #0286 → #0035. #0532 cancels #0286, so #0035 stands and removes #0014.
- **#0009 (−$233K) is withdrawn.** #1018 cancels #0075, so #0056 stands and removes #0009.

About 120 budget updates end up withdrawn this way. Examples include #0006, #0008, #0027, #0028, #0099, #0167 and #0262. Long chains like #0473 (five levels deep, ending in withdrawal) were resolved the same way.

**Pass 2: apply the remaining updates in order.**

- I started from the $1630K set in #0001.
- I then applied every Finance Office increase or decrease that was not withdrawn.
- I ignored messages from other teams, since only the Finance Office can change the budget.
- I also ignored Finance Office notes that don't change the budget, such as room moves, audit notes and cost-center codes.

Some running totals along the way:

| After record | Budget |
|---|---|
| #0024 | $1795K |
| #0461 | $2194K |
| #0804 | $3251K |
| #1138 | $2063K |
| #1333 | $418K |
| #1600 | $1528K |

This was a long hand calculation over about 1,600 records, so a small arithmetic slip is possible.

ANSWER: $1528K
